title: Chapter Review: Data Models and Storage Engines

questions.prompt: A recommendation engine needs "customers who bought what you bought, up to three hops away." Which model fits?
Which change is the classic downside of denormalization?
options: Renaming a product means updating every copy

questions.prompt: An append-only log makes writes sequential.
A Bitcask store has 10 billion keys and 32 GB of RAM. What's the problem?
options: The hash index of every key won't fit in memory

questions.prompt: Which structure lets an LSM-tree skip segments that can't contain a key?

options: They're sorted, so it's a linear merge like mergesort

questions.prompt: What's the in-memory sorted buffer of recent writes in an LSM-tree called? (one word)
A B-tree with 4 KB pages and a branching factor of 500 has four levels. Roughly how much can it store?
Which engine gives more predictable read latency?
Both B-trees and LSM-trees write data more than once.
A dashboard sums revenue by region over 500 million sales. Which storage fits?
What does the query optimizer do?
options: Decides how to run a declarative query: which index, which join order
